methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $100M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ocean Infinity, a growth-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Oliver Plunkett, has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a limited comparable universe: one identified private peer (Orbital Marine Power) and no public ocean-tech benchmarks, reflecting the nascent nature of the frontier-maritime sector.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Using the $100M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, this method yields $120M. The implied range spans $102M (low) to $138M (high), with $120M as the median point. This relatively tight band reflects the single methodological input available and the absence of revenue or earnings multiples to cross-check.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, centered on $120M. Key uncertainties are material: the comp set remains extremely sparse, reliant on one private peer with likely different capital intensity and revenue profiles; no public market data exists to calibrate sector multiples; and the stage-progression multiplier itself carries execution risk. Revenue scale, unit economics, and path to positive cash flow would be necessary to refine this range materially. Additional private peer data or disclosure of Ocean Infinity's own financial metrics would improve confidence substantially.
